children: Crude oil futures gave back some gains Wednesday, a day after surging to four-month highs, as reports suggested Saudi Arabia was offering additional crude cargoes ​through Oman, easing a bit of the concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

Saudi Arabia is offering more crude loadings to Asian refiners through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port, which is outside the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported, in an effort to lessen the impact on supply from attacks on the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.

) has offered its flagship Arab Light grade, as well as Arab Medium and Arab Heavy, to term buyers in Asia for loading off Sohar, indicating it is moving more crude out of the ​Persian Gulf for onward transfer outside Hormuz, the report said.
) reportedly has doubled daily crude loadings at its Ras Tanura ​and Juaymah terminals inside the Gulf to ~4M barrels over the past week, according to satellite tracking.
"News around Saudi Arabia exporting from the Gulf suggests concerns that the disruption could be larger are easing," ​UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said in a note.

) is seeking to return about half the capacity of its East-West pipeline within days, working to bypass a damaged section on the route, and is looking to return the conduit to its full capability in roughly six weeks.
U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox Business that flows crude and related products through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 11M bbl/day during the previous seven days.
Oil prices were further pressured Wednesday after the U.S. Energy Information Administration reported a smaller-than-expected draw from domestic crude inventories last week.

Commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by 640K barrels to 423.4M barrels in the week ended September 11 and were 1% above the five-year average for the time of year, the EIA said.

U.S. gasoline inventories increased by 794K barrels to 207.7M barrels and were 5% below the five-year average, and distillate fuel stocks rose by 1.6M barrels to 107.9M barrels and were 13% below the five-year average for the time of year.

for November delivery tumbled 2.7% to $105.83/bbl, after both benchmarks settled the previous session at the highest since May 19.
